page.layout: One page of text, verse set in italic, no margin notes. Below the text: a signature at the centre foot and a catchword at the lower right.

l.i: Quod se vix notis juuenem commiserit undis
Et tot pertulerit duro sub Rege labores,
Callaicum videt Ascanium quem diuitis auri
Impulerat malesuada fames confidere ponto,
Nunc piget: Ergo locum insidijs tempusque nocendo
Nactus in Hispalici faciem se vertit Abantis
Dux Erebi, torui(s)que rubentia lumina flammis
Velaque pennarum, & furiales exuit artus,
Militis assimulat formam procul ardet in armis
Aureus, aurata volitant in casside plumae
Aurea atra humeris, lateri micat aureus ensis,
Mox prior Ascanium aggreditur dictisque furorem
Vipereum inspirat: Jam cursum luna peregit
Cum ferimur pelago, & fugientem quaerimus
orbem, Atque utinam nobis lux illa extrema fuisset
Visa mari quae prima fuit, quando omnia retro
In peius ruere, & Patriam spes cassa videndi;
O miseri, mala nostra omnes vicere timores,
Nam quid ego ventos, tempestatemque procacem
Quae Cererem tumidis omnem pene obruit undis,
Et penitus puri corrupit munera Bacchi,
Quid memorem rapido conuulsam turbine classem?
Aspice adhuc tantae superant monumenta ruinae;
Nec satis en etiam ceu nos incommoda rerum
Nulla agitent, miseras urget penuria naues
Quae iam quassatae pelagoque annisque fatiscunt
Nusquam certa domus, terris prohibemur, & alto;

page.notes: Verse printed in italic without stanza breaks, so the whole passage is one paragraph. Some letters are doubtful in the scan: "torui(s)que" is a reading of a worn word, and "Callaicum" and "Hispalici" are as printed. Long s is given as s throughout. The Greek and Latin "&" is kept as printed. The catchword "Vera" is at the lower right. The signature "B 3" is at the centre foot. A faint mark at the lower left is not printed text.
